result.topic_en: Gauss studies the primitive (proper) roots of x^n - 1 = 0 for composite n with distinct prime factors, the cyclotomic quotient X giving them, its value at x = 1, the numbers of factors in its numerator and denominator, and conditions on the degree of rational factors of X, with a lemma on congruences modulo a prime p = kb + 1.

die Nenner $\nu + \frac{\nu \cdot \nu - 1 \cdot \nu - 2}{1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3} +$

Factoren oder in jedem $2^{\nu - 1}$

dessen Coefficienten rat: waren

1) dass $\lambda$ durch $a^{\alpha-1}(a-1)$, $b^{\beta-1}(b-1)$, $c^{\gamma-1}(c-1)$ u.s.w. theilbar seyn müsste

so wird $(a + bk + ck^2 + dk^3 \ldots)^b$ nothwendig nicht $\equiv 0$ (mod. p, $x^{b-1} + x^{b-2} \ldots$) seyn können.

methods.what: Cyclotomic polynomial for n with distinct prime factors via inclusion–exclusion product of x^d - 1

methods.what: Value of the cyclotomic polynomial at x=1: 1 if several prime factors, a if n is a prime power
methods.quote: der Werth von X für $x = 1$ wird $=$ [-1-] wenn mehrere [?] Factoren in [?] ggf. [?] n, oder $= a$ wenn $n = a^\alpha$

methods.what: Number of factors in numerator and denominator equals 2^(ν-1) (sums of even/odd binomial coefficients)
Divisibility condition on the degree of a rational factor of X
methods.quote: dass $\lambda$ durch $a^{\alpha-1}(a-1)$, $b^{\beta-1}(b-1)$, $c^{\gamma-1}(c-1)$ u.s.w. theilbar seyn müsste

methods.what: Proof via raising to the power kb+1 (Fermat-type congruence) that coefficients must be congruent
methods.quote:
Bew. wäre $(a + bk + ck^2 +)^b \equiv 0$ so wäre auch $(a + bk + ck^2 +)^{bk+1} \equiv 0$ aber jenes Potenz ist
$\equiv a + bk + ck^2 +$ etc. $\equiv (b-a)k + (c-a)k^2 +$ etc. folglich müsste seyn $a \equiv b \equiv c$ etc.

items.quote:
Wenn X einen Factor vom Grade $\lambda$ hätte so lässt sich zeigen
1) dass $\lambda$ durch $a^{\alpha-1}(a-1)$, $b^{\beta-1}(b-1)$, $c^{\gamma-1}(c-1)$ u.s.w. theilbar seyn müsste
items.english: If X had a factor of degree λ, one can show 1) that λ would have to be divisible by a^(α-1)(a-1), b^(β-1)(b-1), c^(γ-1)(c-1), etc.

items.quote:
2) dass ferner auch die Factor, deren Wurzeln alle eigentl. Wurzeln der Gl. $x^{b^\beta c^\gamma d^\delta \ldots} - 1 = 0$
sind einen Factor der Dimension $\frac{\lambda}{a^{\alpha-1}(a-1)}$ haben müsste
items.english: 2) that furthermore the factor whose roots are all proper roots of x^(b^β c^γ d^δ…) - 1 = 0 would have to have a factor of dimension λ/(a^(α-1)(a-1)), whose coefficients could be expressed rationally in a root of x^(a^α) - 1 = 0.

items.quote: Um dem beweisen würden folgende Hülfssaetze ausreichen [?]
items.english: To prove this, the following lemmas would suffice.

items.quote:
I. Wenn a, b, c, d bc. ganze Zahlen sind, k Wurzel der Gl. $x^b - 1 = 0$ d. p Primzahl $= kb + 1$
so wird $(a + bk + ck^2 + dk^3 \ldots)^b$ nothwendig nicht $\equiv 0$ (mod. p, $x^{b-1} + x^{b-2} \ldots$) seyn können.
items.english: I. If a, b, c, d etc. are integers, k a root of x^b - 1 = 0 and p a prime = kb + 1, then (a + bk + ck^2 + dk^3 …)^b necessarily cannot be ≡ 0 (mod p, x^(b-1) + x^(b-2) …).

items.quote: daraus scheint aber folgen $a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + \ldots - ab - bc -$ etc. $\equiv 0$ (mod. pp)
items.english: From this, however, it seems to follow that a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + … - ab - bc - etc. ≡ 0 (mod pp).
